## Rating

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple" title="Met"}
The package is deposited in a repository that commits to preserving it for a stated period (e.g. at least five years after publication), AND the README states how the code will stay runnable over time, e.g. an archived computing environment (container image), a maintenance plan, or reliance on free/open-source software whose versions remain obtainable.
:::
::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple" title="Partially met"}
The package is preserved (e.g. in a trusted repository), but nothing is done to keep it runnable as software changes (no archived environment, no maintenance plan, reliance on software versions that may disappear); or a maintenance plan exists but the files sit in a place without a preservation commitment (e.g. a personal GitHub account or website only).
:::
::: {.callout-important appearance="simple" title="Not met"}
No preservation commitment and no provision for future executability, e.g. files only on a personal website or 'available upon request'.
:::

[Based on: [#3](../../sources.qmd#p3 "Reproducing statistical results") persistence/longevity, [#42](../../sources.qmd#p42 "AEA data and code availability policy") \>=5-year commitment, [#44](../../sources.qmd#p44 "Active maintenance: a proposal for the long-term computational reproducibility of scientific results") 'active maintenance' plan, [#38](../../sources.qmd#p38 "Ten simple rules for writing dockerfiles for reproducible data science") rebuild containers regularly, [#139](../../sources.qmd#p139 "PRIMAD-LID: a developed framework for computational reproducibility") FOSS, [#143](../../sources.qmd#p143 "What is Computational Reproducibility?") deprecated library versions.]{.source-note}

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Not applicable"}
Never.
:::
